text:
sanjay: Quick RFC follow-up re: token attribution + audit trail for billing. Punted a few edge-cases in the doc, want to capture tradeoffs before we lock schema. https://redwood.internal/rfcs/usage-attribution

anya: +1. We need to pick one of the patterns: 1) synchronous attribution in request path, 2) async post-processing by events. Both have pros/cons.

kevin: async wins on cost/latency but complicates correctness for retries/duplicates. We must guarantee idempotency and deterministic attribution mapping.

elaine: Also need tamper-evidence for audits. Billing teams will want signed receipts or append-only store with proofs for a month at least.

kevin: For duplicates, use request_id + idempotency_key in the event schema. Dedup window = 24h? open to shorter if storage cost matters.

anya: Draft schema suggestion (for discussion):
```json
{
  "event_type": "generation",
  "event_id": "evt_XXXXX",
  "request_id": "req_YYYYY",
  "idempotency_key": "idem_abc",
  "account_id": "acct_123",
  "model": "rw-gpt-3-small",
  "input_tokens": 42,
  "output_tokens": 128,
  "timestamp": 1719004321,
  "attribution": "dedicated|hosted|private",
  "route_metadata": "pool=b,gpu_type=A"
}
```

sanjay: Nice. Two follow-ups: (A) attribution precedence when multiple tenants appear in a single request (e.g., proxy + final user), (B) what level of granularity for token breakdown (per-prompt vs token-stream).

elaine: For multi-tenant, we should record primary_account + secondary_accounts[]. Billing will charge primary_account, but audit trail must show secondary contributors. Keep it explicit rather than inferred.

kevin: Agreed. Storage implication: secondary_accounts as an array increases event size. Could instead store pointers to a small join table. But that complicates async processing.

ops-watchdog: FYI: we already have 2 incidents where async attribution lag produced wrong day-of-month billing. Ops would prefer bounded consistency SLA (e.g., <5m for 95% of events) for hosted customers.

anya: That pushes us toward hybrid: synchronous shallow attribution (primary fields) in request path, and async enrichment (secondary accounts, provenance) in pipeline. So billing can run off the shallow fields for near-real-time, and deep audits use enriched events.

kevin: Implementation notes: event envelope should include an "enrichment_state" enum: {raw, enriched, signed}. Post-processor marks enriched and computes HMAC receipt.

elaine: HMAC receipts are good for tamper evidence. We should sign batches and store signatures in the audit index. Proposal: daily/rolling signatures per customer key.

sanjay: How about idempotency and dedup semantics? Suggest we dedup on event_id at ingestion and persist original event_id + ingestion_ts. Also keep a small tombstone table for 30 days.

kevin: SQL sketch:
```sql
INSERT INTO usage_events(event_id, payload, received_at)
VALUES($1, $2, now())
ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING;
```
This keeps ingestion simple and cheap.

anya: For billing accuracy we need deterministic aggregation path. Recommend materialized view daily_agg(account_id, date, input_tokens, output_tokens) refreshed incrementally. Also add smoothed counters for distributed duplicates.

elaine: Retention: keep raw events 90 days, enriched events 365 days, and signatures/receipts 5 years for enterprise customers. Need product signoff on cost.

ops-watchdog: Alerting: track enrichment lag (time between raw->enriched). Alert if median > 2m or p95 > 10m.

kevin: Edge-case: long-running streamed generations where tokens arrive after initial event. Two options: emit partial events per chunk (token_delta) vs emit final consolidated event when stream closes. Partial events are simpler for live dashboards but complicate billing.

anya: Recommendation: emit partial events with unique chunk_ids and also emit a final reconciliation event. Billing runs on final events; dashboards can use partial for near-real-time.

elaine: Make sure final reconciliation has a finalization flag and final totals. That lets us overwrite/adjust billed totals if reconciliation changes.

sanjay: Action items: (1) update RFC with hybrid attribution model and enrichment_state enum (owner: anya) (2) spike HMAC-signed receipts + key rotation plan (owner: elaine) (3) prototype dedup/tombstone approach in ingestion (owner: kevin) (4) add enrichment lag alerts (owner: ops-watchdog).

anya: I'll update the RFC and add schema diff. Will include sample event sizes so finance can estimate cost.

kevin: I'll start a spike branch and wire up the ON CONFLICT ingestion.

elaine: I'll draft the receipts design and key rotation doc.

billing-bot: Note: billing queue length currently 12, backlog ~3m. Flagging for visibility. :warning:

sanjay: Thanks all. If nobody objects, we'll fold these changes into the RFC by EOD tomorrow and schedule a quick design review on Friday.

kevin: ack

anya: ack

elaine: ack

ops-watchdog: ack
